cards.title: Apple Developing Its Own AI Agent for Mac
cards.body: Apple is building AI agents to compete with Meta Muse, Claude, and OpenAI's offerings. The move signals the tech giant's commitment to the rapidly growing AI agent market.

cards.title: Anthropic Founders Cash Out $2B in Record IPO
cards.body: Anthropic's seven founders each pocketed $280 million at the upgraded $83/share IPO price. The company raised nearly $105 billion in the record-breaking offering.

cards.title: Meta's Muse Charm Wearable Could Cost $300
cards.body: Meta's upcoming AI wearable device may carry a $300 price tag, according to reports from The Information. The company has not denied the reporting, only stating it will share more details soon.

cards.title: Tech Outages Mirror Y2K-Style AI Agent Crisis
cards.body: Recent airline, banking, and productivity platform outages may be linked to deeper systemic issues, according to cybersecurity experts. The incidents suggest potential coordination rather than coincidence.

cards.title: Jensen Huang Resigns from Nvidia Amid Scandal
cards.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has stepped down following personal controversies that could impact U.S.-China AI development competition. The resignation raises national security concerns as both nations race for AI supremacy.

cards.title: Anthropic IPO Could Deliver $156B to Charity
cards.body: At $95 per share, Anthropic's Public Benefit Foundation, employee donations, and company match could total $156 billion. The commitment reflects the company's dedication to responsible AI development.

cards.title: Google's Gemini Agent Now Controls Your Mac
cards.body: Google rolled out AI agent capabilities to Gemini on macOS, enabling file organization, form filling, and multistep workflows. The update marks a major expansion of Google's AI agent ecosystem.

cards.title: Meta's Muse Agent Leaking Private User Data
cards.body: Employees reported Muse surfacing unrelated messages about childcare, career advice, and bank account balances. The data exposure represents a critical privacy vulnerability in Meta's new AI agent.

cards.title: Everful Raises $48.5M for Factory Sourcing Platform
cards.body: The former Alibaba exec's startup secured funding to expand its factory-direct sourcing platform. Everful connects retailers with Chinese manufacturers to streamline overseas product sourcing.

cards.title: Anthropic Hits Nasdaq at $111, Up 33%
cards.body: Anthropic's stock opened 33% above its $83 IPO price, reaching $111 on the first day of trading. The offering raised over $80 billion in new capital for the AI frontier lab.

cards.title: Anthropic CEO Reaffirms Commitment to Pacing AI
cards.body: Dario Amodei used Nasdaq's opening bell ceremony to reiterate Anthropic's dedication to responsible AI development. The commitment stands firm regardless of business or political pressures.

cards.title: Anthropic IPO Tests AI's Circular Financing Boom
cards.body: Despite massive compute commitments as a public company, Anthropic's infrastructure partners Amazon and Google profit regardless of outcomes. The arrangement raises questions about competitive dynamics in AI development.

cards.title: Superhuman Pushes Go Agent Into More Products
cards.body: Superhuman is making Go its central AI agent and expanding it to Docs and Mail. The move deepens the assistant's integration across the company's product suite.

cards.title: Microsoft CEO Explains 60K Voluntary Buyout Offer
cards.body: Satya Nadella offered buyouts to 60,000 employees in October, urging them to voluntarily quit rather than face layoffs. The move is driven by AI strategy, though not in the traditional sense.

cards.title: Nadella Warns Critical Infrastructure is Unpatchable
cards.body: Microsoft's CEO noted that much critical infrastructure cannot be patched, creating vulnerability to AI-enabled cyberattacks. The challenge presents both security risks and opportunities for tech companies.

cards.title: Musk Compares Huang Ouster to Losing Michael Jordan
cards.body: Elon Musk defended Jensen Huang, saying his departure is like kicking Michael Jordan off your team. Musk stressed he doesn't believe Huang is disloyal to the United States.

cards.title: Nadella Confident in Nvidia After Huang's Exit
cards.body: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella expressed confidence in Colette Kress, who is serving as Nvidia's interim CEO. The statement signals continued partnership between the two tech giants.

cards.title: AI Agents Could Disrupt Web's Advertising Economy
cards.body: Satya Nadella predicts AI agents will fundamentally reshape how companies compete for customers online. The shift could force Amazon and other ad-driven platforms to rethink their business models.

cards.title: Anthropic Prices IPO at $83, Above Projections
cards.body: Anthropic's long-awaited IPO priced above the originally projected range at $83 per share. The valuation reaches $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

cards.title: Nvidia Delays Routine SEC Quarterly Report Filing
cards.body: Nvidia announced it won't file its formal quarterly 10-Q report for several weeks, creating unusual intrigue on Wall Street. The delay prompted analysts to investigate the unexpected announcement.

cards.title: The AI Hype Index: AI is everywhere
cards.body: AI has become ubiquitous across industries and consumer products. From Google's AI Overviews to AI-powered humanoid robots, the technology is spreading rapidly despite concerns about implementation costs and effectiveness.

cards.title: This smell startup says its AI nose is as good as a human's
cards.body: A New Jersey lab is training AI to recognize odors by collecting data from experienced human sniffers. The startup aims to create an AI system that can match human olfactory capabilities using chemical analysis and descriptive training data.

cards.title: LLMs will get climate info wrong if you ask
cards.body: Large language models can confidently provide incorrect information about climate topics. Users should verify AI-generated climate data through authoritative sources rather than relying solely on LLM responses.

cards.title: Will Wright's next simulation uses AI to mine memories
cards.body: Designer Will Wright is developing MyMems, an AI-driven simulation that extracts content from users' personal memories. The project represents an inward turn for simulation technology, focusing on individual experience and data.
